title: AutoGen tool orchestration
text: AutoGen emphasizes programmable multi-agent orchestration. Agents can be configured with explicit tool or function calls, and a manager-style workflow can coordinate planning, execution, tool use, and review across multiple participants.

title: AutoGen group collaboration
text: AutoGen supports group-style multi-agent collaboration where different agents can hold specialized roles. This makes it suitable for tasks that require workflow control, tool execution, code execution, or human-in-the-loop review.

title: CAMEL communicative agents
text: CAMEL focuses on role-playing and communicative agents. Its typical setup uses role definitions and conversational interaction to explore tasks, making it useful for studying autonomous interaction patterns and open-ended dialogue.

title: CAMEL tool integration profile
text: Compared with orchestration-first frameworks, CAMEL's core emphasis is less on explicit external tool scheduling and more on role-conditioned communication. Tool use can be added, but it is not the central architectural primitive in the basic role-playing formulation.

title: RAG evidence grounding
text: A retrieval-augmented generation workflow can provide explicit evidence passages before answer synthesis. In a verifiable multi-agent system, a Researcher node can retrieve passages, an Executor can draft from them, and a Verifier can audit whether claims are grounded in retrieved evidence.
